LESSON: SUBTRACTION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.4: Subtraction
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Subtraction, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do you subtract a one-digit number from a two-digit number?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Model subtraction using concrete objects in purposive pairs/groups. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology to carry out the activity of modelling. Safety of all learners should be observed especially for learners with chronic health conditions.

2. Use ' - ' and '=' signs in writing subtraction sentences in purposive pairs/groups.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Model subtraction using concrete objects in purposive pairs/groups. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or appropriate assistive technology to carry out the activity of modelling. Safety of all learners should be observed especially for learners with chronic health conditions.
2. Use ' - ' and '=' signs in writing subtraction sentences in purposive pairs/groups.
3. Subtract by counting backwards. Learners with speech difficulties could use

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Subtraction together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: learner learns subtraction of numbers by counting backwards.

● Creativity: learner creates patterns involving subtraction.

Values:
● Responsibility: learner takes care of concrete objects used in subtraction.

● Unity: learner shares number cards or charts as they work out subtraction.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Social cohesion: learner works with peers to create patterns involving subtraction.

● Critical thinking: learner works out subtraction by counting backwards.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the skills of writing subtraction sentences to functional writing in English Language Activities.
